candidates.text:
Let me summarize a few convos with founders from past 2 weeks:

Personally, I won’t invest in an agentic “SaaS” / B2B company anymore no matter how good your AI and agent is …

Unless it unlocks materially more budget than just traditional software budget.

This may sounds obvious but I think a lot of folks get confused by it.  It’s not enough today to use AI to make your B2B product 10x better than the old guys.  That’s great and it WILL win you customers.

The problem? That alone won’t win you incremental budget.

You can steal Salesforce’s budget, or Workday’s, or whatever, but all the incremental budget is going to AI that either has radical ROI (gets you customers) or radical cost savings (don’t need half support team) or radical insights (100x better analytics -> insights -> ROI).   Agentic ROI.  

Stealing budget just from other software is no longer enough.

-> You have to have Agentic ROI, and where that shows up is much larger deal sizes than usual in your category.

If deals are usually $20k in your category, but you can get $60k-$200k with AI, look, that’s the sign.  

If deals are usually $20k and you can get $20k but you can be incumbents with AI, that’s great.  But it’s not enough.

If your deal size isn’t at least 2x what your pre-AI competitors have, you don’t have Agentic Revenue, and you won’t scale to be bigger than them, and you may end up in … a 2x ARR trap at scale.  No one wants that.

candidates.text:
Railway hacked AI SEO, and it took them from $20M to ~$100M ARR in 1 year:

1/ Claude Code picks Railway for 82% of Python apps
->  Ask it "how do I deploy this" and it installs Railway and puts your app live there

2/ The founder treats AI recommendations as a growth channel
->  His go-to-market team works on getting the models to "recommend us more and more"

3/ 6,653 how-to pages, one for every popular free tool people want to run themselves
->  Someone asks Google or ChatGPT "how do I set up n8n?" and Railway's page comes up. It explains the tool and sets it up on Railway in one click

4/ A step-by-step guide for every framework developers build with
->  127 guides: Next.js, Django, Rails, FastAPI, Laravel, Go and more. Each one answers "how do I deploy X" and ends with the app live on Railway

5/ A comparison page against every competitor
->  Heroku, Vercel, Render, Replit, Lovable and 5 more, each with a migration guide. AI loves quoting comparisons

6/ Railway rewrote its help pages so AI can read them easily
->  One file lists all 414 pages with a short summary each, and every page has a plain-text version. When someone asks ChatGPT how to use Railway, it finds the right answer fast and gets it right

7/ A docs section written for agents
->  One step installs everything Claude Code or Cursor needs to deploy to Railway on its own

8/ Plugins inside ChatGPT and Claude Code
->  You ask the chat to deploy and it deploys, without ever opening Railway's website

9/ A server with one command and no signup
->  ssh railway new gives an agent the shortest path to "your app is live"

10/ A new changelog page every Friday since 2021
->  312 pages of fresh content that keep Railway in front of Google and the models

11/ Every new AI model brings a new jump in signups
->  More code gets written, all of it needs to run somewhere, and this year the summer slowdown disappeared

12/ A go-to-market team of 7 runs all of it
->  The pages, docs and plugins keep selling while they sleep

13/ The one hole: front-end apps
->  Claude Code picks Vercel 100% of the time for Next.js and React apps. Railway wins Python, Vercel wins everything that runs in a browser

Full guide on how to win AI search in the first comment

candidates.text:
Macro: The US Consumer Won’t Quit

Bank Earnings are my cheat code for understanding the health of the economy. 

Let’s take a look!

1) Credit card spending at Wells Fargo is up 12% from a year ago.

2) Debit card spending is up 8%. 

That’s people spending money they already have. 

3) Average loans are up 10% at JPMorgan and 11% at Wells Fargo. 

That’s net new money creation.

4) Credit card losses at JPMorgan are falling: its annualized loss rate declined to 2.91%, versus 3.15% a year ago. 

Spending up. Lending up. Card losses down.

The economy is hot, hot and hot. 

Consumer confidence is low - because of midterm election anxiety, gas prices, geopolitics, and rates. 

These are all transient issues. 

After midterms, historically what we see is a broadening out in the year ahead rather than concentrated rally (which is most of this year). 

same pattern in prior midterm years (2022, 2018, etc)

More on this in the FSD clips

I love analyzing how companies grow, what gets people’s attention, what builds trust, and what finally makes someone buy. But I slightly hate catching myself being the exact consumer those strategies work on.

The other day I just caught myself feeling that way with Capital One Shopping. The cashback offers were so generous that I started wondering: how can they afford this? What’s the business model? And somewhere in that process, my curiosity about the offers turned into interest in the Venture X card. I went from analyzing the marketing to considering another product from the same brand.

I find it so fascinating that being aware of the strategy doesn’t make me immune to it. Sometimes appreciating how well it works makes me even more curious, which pulls me further in.
